summary: This January 2026 immigration lecture is already-public Game Theory, Education, and Meritocracy support: Jiang treats immigration as a host-written game where school success, income, legality, and politeness can leave immigrants useful inside another group's rules without status or command.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The apparent immigrant success story breaks when the invited player accepts a casino game written by the house; whoever writes the rules keeps status, power, money, and talent flows.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Game Theory page already carries this source in the Host-Written Rules section, and the episode read already links exact marks to the durable lens point.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Grades, technical skill, compliance, income, and respectable work can make East Asian and Indian immigrants legible to school and employment without giving them command over status games.
existing_lens_links.rationale: Education and Meritocracy already use this source to separate school success, credentials, and income from social command. The episode read already links the exact school-status marks.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: No public append is needed. Keep this source as the host-written-rules mechanism: playing well by the visible rules differs from authoring the game, and the house can praise immigrant success while preserving command of status, talent extraction, and the definition of winning.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Game Theory owns rule authorship, payoff tables, and host-written games. Nation owns political-body conflict and demographic cohesion; Education owns school formation; Meritocracy owns credential limits.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: school can train obedience, focus, caution, grades, and technical competence for one reward system while the wider social game rewards risk, articulation, assertiveness, collaboration, and command.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Education should not become a general immigration page. Its active mechanism is school formation producing useful, respectable players who may still lack status and command.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: credentials can certify competence and obedience without granting status. This source supplies the immigration/status correction after earlier elite-school wound-to-credential material.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Meritocracy owns the credential's limit and backward pressure. Game Theory owns the host-written rule structure that makes the credential subordinate.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only as bounded Nation pressure if a future immigration/demography section is reviewed: Jiang frames immigration anxiety as conflict over which population becomes the future political body, but this source does not by itself justify an Immigration, Replacement, or Demographic War public page.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Nation owns the collective-body and future-majority question. Game Theory owns the host-written game; Prediction owns dated claims about Europe, America, and violent demographic conflict.

new_lens_seeds.title: Demographic Cohesion Breaks Host-Written Rules
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Jiang's proposed immigrant counter-game is not better assimilation into the host's scoreboard but group cohesion, religion, language, and fertility that can make descendants numerous enough to write the next game.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as sensitive routing pressure only. It may later belong under Nation, Game Theory, or Gerontocracy if multiple dated sources show the same mechanism; do not create a standalone public page from this lecture alone.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang explicitly connects immigration to the recurring game-theory distinction between playing by rules and writing rules: the host can invite immigrants into a game whose visible rewards do not include command.

Jiang states 2050-oriented demographic pressure claims for Europe and the United States, including Muslim fertility in Europe, Hispanic growth in America, and violent conflict if the American-led open immigration game becomes unsustainable.

Jiang personalizes the status thesis by saying that money in America was possible for him but high status was not, and that leaving America was his own response to being stuck inside the host-written game.

canon_candidates.claim: The open immigration game becomes unsustainable and produces future violent demographic conflict as younger, cohesive, higher-fertility immigrant groups challenge aging host populations.
canon_candidates.boundary_note: Split Europe Muslim-demography, U.S. Hispanic-demography, American talent-extraction/globalization, and generalized violent-conflict branches before any ledger scoring or public canon promotion.

next_actions.note: Do not create standalone Immigration Game, Immigration Trap, Replacement, Muslim Europe, Hispanic America, East Asian Men, Model Minority, OkCupid, DEI, or Demographic War pages from this source alone.

If later sources cluster around immigration/demography, write a concept-scoped Nation/Game Theory boundary review before any public prose; include source sensitivity and avoid turning topic labels into concepts.
Only promote prediction material after splitting Europe, United States, demographic replacement, globalization/talent extraction, and violence-horizon claims into separately falsifiable records.
